verdict.rationale: Mem0's own webhooks let users register URLs that receive automatic HTTP POST requests when memories are created, updated, deleted, or categorized. This is a first-party event-to-action trigger. However, nothing documents a rules engine with conditions, filters, or configurable actions beyond the outbound callback, so downstream logic must live in the user's own receiver. Missing for 10: user-definable rule conditions or filters, built-in actions beyond HTTP POST notifications, documentation of rule configuration depth, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can configure webhooks to send HTTP POST requests to your specified URLs whenever memories are created, updated, deleted, or categorized.
Webhooks enable real-time notifications for memory events in your Mem0 project.
